brief: Slovakia's private systemic banks form a dense, highly regular disclosure landscape: every bank must publish under Opatrenie NBS č. 16/2014 plus CRR Part Eight, so SLSP, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB and 365.bank each maintain a Pillar 3 / 'zverejňovanie informácií' series with predictable, date-stamped PDF filenames that are well suited to templated harvesting (VÚB and ČSOB are the cleanest). The higher-value stream for deadline intelligence is the contractual layer: statutory two-month pre-notice of T&C changes produces dated 'oznámenie o zmene / prehľad zmien / navrhované zmeny' documents — Tatra banka and ČSOB even publish explicit before/after change logs — which pin exactly when a rule bites in retail practice (e.g. instant-payment limits, accessibility-act clauses, 2026 fee schedules). Everything is Slovak-only in practice, with no RSS or API anywhere, so collection must be scheduled diffing plus own snapshot archiving; parent-group disclosures (Erste, Intesa, RBI, KBC) serve as an earlier, English-language leading indicator. Main open gaps are smaller banks and foreign-bank branches, specialised disclosure types (remuneration, ESG, MREL), and the absence of vendor-side historical archives.
